text:
jordan: heads up — our p4d / p5d reserved coverage in us-west-2 just dropped ~18% vs last quarter, looks like a mixture of decommissions and tag drift. Savings Plans expire in ~45 days for the largest commit. :eyes:
maria: yikes. do we have a breakdown by instance family & tag? can we surface which clusters freed capacity?
kevin: quick check — ran the coverage query against billing export. main hit is `redwood-training-prod` cluster, some nodes were terminated during the jan infra refresh. also ~120 hours of untagged GPU usage over jan-feb. snippet: ```SELECT line_item_resource_id, product_instance_type, sum(usage_amount) as hours FROM billing WHERE product = 'EC2' AND usage_type LIKE '%GPU%' GROUP BY 1,2 ORDER BY hours DESC LIMIT 10;```
natalie: ops-bot just posted an automated alert: "Reserved coverage fell below 85% for GPU family p4d in us-west-2" — timestamped 2053456702.
jordan: thanks. proposal: stagger renewal windows to avoid simultaneous renewals across families and regions. also recommend converting a portion of the upcoming SP to regional zonal RIs for predictable baseline throughput.
maria: can we quantify the cost delta? rough numbers: current commit saves us ~$1.2M/yr; 18% lost coverage is ~216k/yr in increased spend if workload stays same. converting 30% to zonal RIs buys latency guarantees for dedicated pools but reduces SP flexibility.
kevin: i sketched a small model — attached as inline table: ```optionA: convert 30% to zonal => +$40k annual net savings vs status quo assuming steady utilization
optionB: keep SP but buy short-term reservations for hot clusters => up-front $110k exchange fee risk
optionC: do nothing and try to reclaim tag drift => variable risk```
natalie: reclaiming tag drift is low-hanging fruit. we should run a sweep to identify terminated vs active instances missing costcenter tags. i can run an IAM-tagging enforcement job next week.
jordan: agreed. quick triage steps: 1) reclaimable = terminated instances still showing as reserved attachments? 2) identify long-running ephemeral jobs that now run on on-demand 3) propose renewal staggering schedule.
kevin: for (1) i ran `aws ec2 describe-reserved-instances --filters Name=state,Values=active` and cross-referenced with instance usage — a handful of RIs pinned to old AZs. we could do partial exchange but need CFO signoff for churn.
maria: action item: natalie to run tag-sweep (due 2026-03-25). kevin to prototype exchange scenarios and a worst-case cost model (due 2026-03-22). jordan to draft staggered renewal calendar & playbook (due 2026-03-24). I'll loop in finance after kevin's model. :thumbsup:
ops-bot: scheduled job created: `tag-sweep-v2` will run 2026-03-20 02:00 UTC and output CSV to s3://redwood-ops/ri-audit/2053456789-sweep.csv
natalie: noted. i'll include a flag to auto-attach a remediation ticket for untagged active instances.
jordan: one more operational note — if we convert part of the SP to zonal RIs, we should pin critical inference fleets to the reserved pool and route less critical jobs to burst/spot to preserve latency SLOs.
maria: good plan. can we also add a dashboard tile that shows "coverage by family x region" with a 90-day trend and a predicted coverage at current decomm rate? helps decision cadence.
kevin: will add to infra-dashboard backlog. quick query i'll reuse: ```SELECT date_trunc('day', usage_start) as d, product_instance_type, sum(usage_amount) as hours FROM billing WHERE product='EC2' AND usage_type LIKE '%GPU%' GROUP BY 1,2 ORDER BY 1 DESC;```
jordan: thanks all. tagging sweep + kevin's model should give us enough to decide whether to 1) exchange RIs, 2) convert part of SP to zonal, or 3) aggressively reclaim and retry renewal as-is.
maria: if anyone sees sudden spin-ups in us-west-2 over the next week, ping here immediately. i'll pause any discretionary infra refreshes that could change utilization until we close this.
kevin: noted. i'll post the model when ready.
natalie: starting sweep now — will post CSV and top-10 offenders once complete.
ops-bot: job `tag-sweep-v2` completed at 2053457200. s3://redwood-ops/ri-audit/2053456789-sweep.csv (rows=642).
jordan: great, thanks. closing loop once kevin's numbers are in. :white_check_mark:
